transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining the calibration meeting for Taylor's annual performance review. As we all know, the current draft flags some missed deliverables as a concern, and I'd like to make sure we have a complete picture before I finalize the rating and written record. Let's go through our usual round of input. I'd like to hear from the project lead, a peer colleague, and HR. One specific area I want us to address: the final review record should include firsthand examples of Taylor identifying delivery risks early enough for the team to avoid an escalation. If anyone has direct examples of that, please share them so we can make sure they're captured. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important before we go further. My project records show that exactly six of Taylor's delayed deliverables were delayed because leadership reprioritized the work after Taylor had already started it. I haven't yet added this attribution to the calibration notes, but it's directly relevant to the missed deliverables concern flagged in the draft.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I can speak to that specific area, Marisol. I directly observed exactly four occasions when Taylor identified a delivery risk early enough for the team to avoid an escalation. These examples haven't been collected in Taylor's review packet yet, but I can share the details so they're captured in the final review record.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share a confidential HR matter that directly affects this calibration. My HR record confirms that Taylor worked under an approved 80 percent schedule for two months of the review cycle. This means the goals for that period must be recalibrated to 80 percent of standard capacity. The schedule arrangement is confidential, but this is material to fairly assessing the missed deliverables flagged in the draft, and I want to make sure it's accounted for before we finalize.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Grant to add the six reprioritized-delay attributions to the calibration notes so the final review record reflects that those six delayed deliverables were caused by leadership reprioritization, not Taylor's performance.
Nia to provide written details of the four occasions when Taylor identified delivery risks early enough for the team to avoid an escalation, so they are captured in the final review record.
Owen to confirm the recalibrated goal expectations for the two-month approved 80 percent schedule period, ensuring the final review reflects adjusted capacity for that span.

Marisol will revise the draft review to remove the missed-deliverables concern for the six reprioritized items, incorporate the four risk-intervention examples, apply the 80 percent capacity recalibration, and finalize the rating as Meets Expectations.
